title: Huntington's disease: stages over decades
description: Huntington's disease is inherited and caused by a change in a single gene. It develops over decades, so this timeline is in stages, not minutes. Structural MRI is the most sensitive imaging marker of how it progresses, and the striatum, made up of the caudate and putamen, shrinks over the years. In this state the dimming stands for loss of brain tissue, measured as a smaller volume, not for lower activity.
caveat: The stages are built from people at different points before and after symptoms begin, compared with people without the gene change; they are not one person followed through the whole disease. The far-from-onset finding comes from one study of 64 young adults with the gene change, who on average were about 24 years from expected symptoms and whose thinking and mood were normal. How much tissue is lost at each stage is not given in the sources read, so the levels drawn are illustrative. The caudate is drawn on the basis of a review that speaks of the striatum as a whole.

phases.name: Decades before symptoms
phases.caption: Young adults who carry the gene change, on average about 24 years before expected symptoms. Their thinking and mood are normal, and their brain works normally, but the putamen is slightly smaller than in people without the gene change.

phases.name: Approaching symptoms
phases.caption: Closer to expected onset, small changes in movement and thinking begin to show on careful tests, and grey matter volume helps predict who will soon be diagnosed. The striatum continues to shrink.

order.rationale: The stages come from comparing groups at different distances from expected onset, not from following one group all the way.

phases.name: Symptoms begin
phases.caption: Movement, thinking and behaviour change. Nerve cells stop working properly and die; structural MRI is the most sensitive imaging marker of this progression.

order.rationale: From group comparisons and a review of how the disease is tracked, not from following one person.

phases.name: Progression
phases.caption: The disease continues to progress. How far the loss goes at each stage is not given in the sources read; the dimming drawn is illustrative.

order.rationale: The disease is described as progressive; the later stages are not measured in the sources read.

regions.explanation: Slightly smaller in young adults with the gene change about 24 years before expected symptoms, in one study, though how much smaller was not clearly related to how far away symptoms were. Later, the striatum as a whole shrinks over the years. The dimming stands for smaller volume, not lower activity.

The dimming stands for smaller volume, not lower activity.

citations.quote: In mutation carriers, huntingtin is produced with abnormally long polyglutamine sequences that confer toxic gains of function and predispose the protein to fragmentation, resulting in neuronal dysfunction and death.
